title: Understanding and Practice in Accord
author: Zhanran
excerpt: To study Buddhism one must keep understanding and practice in accord; only then can one gain real benefit. Otherwise, it is like counting another’s ten thousand strings of coins while possessing not a single penny oneself. At the same time, understanding is for the sake of practice, and only through practice can understanding go deeper.

inline.s: To study Buddhism one must keep understanding and practice in accord; only then can one gain real benefit.

Otherwise, it is like counting another’s ten thousand strings of coins while having not a single penny oneself. At the same time, understanding is for the sake of practice, and only through practice can one understand more deeply.

Prajna contemplation is the wondrous method for keeping understanding and practice in accord. Through contemplating in accord with principle, one corrects the body (conduct), speech, and mind, and purifies habitual tendencies. Prajna contemplation has two phases: understanding the principle (the middle-way doctrine of neither being nor non-being) and putting it into practice (the practice of non-attachment to marks, with compassion and emptiness practiced together). Understanding the principle is understanding; putting it into practice is practice. Jiang Weinong’s Diamond Sutra Lectures say: “In reading the sutras and hearing the Dharma, one should be deeply vigilant, taking the Buddha’s words as a mirror and using them at all times and in all places to reflect upon oneself. Without contemplating and reflecting, how could delusion be awakened from? This is what is called relying on words and letters to arouse contemplation. When the work of contemplation has gone on long, then, grandly, a mind of vigilance naturally arises—this is the initial awakening, the first opening of the right wisdom inherent in the essence of the principle. Being thus, never retreating and never slackening, the work of contemplation grows deeper and purer day by day. Then what is called the initial awakening is first like the new moon, gradually more light and less darkness; until the full wheel of the moon is complete and its radiance shines forth, then the essence of nature manifests. This is the initial awakening merging with the fundamental awakening, and there is no longer any distinction between the initial and the fundamental. You should know that what is called becoming a Buddha is nothing other than the perfect clarity of the awakened nature. And the opening of that awakened nature depends precisely on the power of the prajna of words and letters—there is no other way. Therefore it is said: all Buddhas are born from this sutra.”
[Jing ti: watchful and wary.] [Huang huang ran: grand and majestic in appearance.]

The Elder Master Xuyun said: ‘The Patriarch Bodhidharma said: “To understand the Buddha-mind, the Essence, and to keep practice in accord with understanding—this is called a Patriarch.” To keep practice and understanding in accord is to be able to speak it and to walk it. … Do not be turned by conditions. It is like herding a cow: you must hold the rope firmly, and when the cow will not obey, give it a few strokes of the whip.
If you can thus constantly subdue your mind

, then as days accumulate and the merit deepens, you will have tidings of the return home.’ ‘When you meet a situation, even what you cannot let go you must still let go; a single stirring of the eyebrow (the slightest thought) already offends against the ancestors’ rule. Having heard the good teacher’s words, do not lose the mirror of awareness. In all things aim at ‘the Way’; the Way is principle. Principle is the mind. What is the mind? The mind is Buddha. The Buddha neither increases nor decreases, is neither blue nor yellow, neither long nor short. As the Diamond Sutra says: “If you see all marks as no marks, you see the Tathagata.” Once you penetrate these lines of reasoning, you are the same as the Buddha. Governing affairs with principle—what matter can you not let go? Reflected in this principle, you put it down at once—‘all marks are false and vain.’ Where do afflictions and right and wrong come from? If you wish to cultivate, what you cannot get through you must still get through—grasp the suchness of the Dharma-nature.” (From the Venerable Xuyun’s Expedient Teachings.)
Question: Delving into Buddhist theory is in fact also very laborious, no easier than actual practice; yet why do many people wallow in theoretical study and never go on to practice?
Answer: It is the head-mind working mischief.
The head-mind
has
two great features: the sense of thirst and the sense of identity. Delving into Buddhist
theory
satisfies both the thirst and the identity-sense of the mind, whereas actual practice leaves the mind without a footing. This is why
many
students of Buddhism sink all their lives into Buddhist
theoretical research
without practicing, unable to apply what they have learned
—which is most regrettable
Therefore, students of Buddhism must be on guard against this tendency to value understanding over practice.
Here is another instruction of the Elder Master Xuyun:

“The lay elder Cen Xuelu, seeking refuge from the Japanese invaders, came to the Dajue Monastery of Yunmen in Ruyuan, and drew near to the Elder Master Xuyun for over a month, and then moved to Lianxian
As he was about to take leave, he bowed and requested an instruction on the essential Dharma. Master Yun laughed and said:

“Lay patron, you have gone deep into the sutra treasury, your wisdom is like the sea, and the Buddha-Dharma within your breast is about to burst your belly. At this point you are like a blind man whose two eyes have regained sight—the road is now seen, and it remains only to walk it yourself. If you yourself do not walk, who will carry you home?” Master Cen, awestruck, bowed, and speedily sent word to Ying (Tang Ying). Ying said:
“Well said!
Master Yun’s words may be said to have shot a whole flock with one arrow!
” (Recorded from the 1963 Gleanings from the Katsuragi Collection, by Rongxi, Malaysian Buddhist Society.)
One can understand even more deeply:
the awakening blow of the Elder Master Xuyun
is to say
: the Buddhist theory that I know, you also know completely. The difference is that I have put it into practice one by one, while you have not. So your problem is no longer listening, but
doing
